notes:
Passed the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level and never a hardware run. The package binds the camera resource of pymodaq_plugins_basler.hardware.basler:BaslerCamera: the model name, detector size, six ROI values, exposure, gain, frame rate, pixel format and grabbing state; six ROI writes through the native set_roi; start/stop grabbing actions; clear_roi; and the native stop_grabbing as the e-stop and the safe-state action. NOT COVERED: the image arrays produced by the pylon image event and consumed by the DAQ viewer (the standard's image form is an artifact reference and this package has no artifact store). NOT COVERED: exposure and gain writes (BaslerCamera has no setter method for them; the DAQ viewer writes the pylon nodes directly, so binding them would bypass the recorded native surface). Limits: every ROI value is Limit.operator_required because no text file of the clone states the usable range of an installed camera; the pylon nodes report GetMin/GetMax only at run time and the sensor size differs by model. site-limits.example.json fills the six paths with placeholder example ranges only, not measurements. The native.py hardware factory was never imported or run; this R1 package does not claim the loader's R2/R3 refusal of an unreviewed model-written hardware backend. Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null).
